voiceover:
[conversational] This social media tool has made over $1M, and it started in Google Sheets.

[curious] And the move that got it going happened before the founder built the software. Stay for that.

It's called Marky. You paste in your website, and it makes a month of on-brand posts, designs the images, and posts to 7 platforms. Small businesses and agencies are who pay for it.

[confident] These numbers are verified on TrustMRR through Stripe. $22K a month in recurring revenue, $16K in the last 30 days, 478 active subscriptions, and 33% month-over-month growth.

So what can you steal? One: let people see the result before they pay. The first 30 posts are free, no card. Two: sell the part competitors skip. Marky designs the image, not just the caption.

[serious] The honest catch? That's revenue, not profit. It's a crowded market. And it's currently listed for sale at $495K.

[whispers] Now the move. He started with Google Sheets, Zapier and about 10 customers, and built the software after that. Find your first paying customer before you write code.

[playful] Would you build this or buy it? Send this to the friend who keeps saying they'll start a business once the app is ready. Hack saved?

topic: Business breakdown: Marky — A tool for self-publishing authors to manage their social media.

pick.topic: Business breakdown: Marky — A tool for self-publishing authors to manage their social media.
pick.angle: A tiny SaaS for self-publishing authors has made over $1M by solving one boring problem: authors hate doing social media

research.what_it_does: You add your website and Marky makes a month of on-brand posts, designs the image in your brand, and posts them to 7 platforms.
research.who_pays: Small businesses and agencies. The Pro plan is for agencies. Agencies can resell Marky under their own brand, with a client portal that carries their logo and colors.
research.pricing: Official pricing page: first 30 posts free, no credit card needed. Solo is $39 a month (1 workspace, 3 channels, 1 user). Growth is $79 a month (5 channels, unlimited users, marked Most Popular). Pro is $229 a month (8 channels, white-label portal). Extra channels cost +$7/mo. The page also advertises $19/month billed annually.
growth: TrustMRR lists the marketing channels as Facebook, Meta Ads, word of mouth and influencers. No source I found gives numbers for any of them.

Early days, in the founder's own Medium post: he started with Google Sheets and Zapier and about 10 customers, and says to find your first paying customer. He also writes that he spent hours a day talking to customers.
In the founder's podcast interview, he describes viewing yourself as a consultant for the first customer, and says that is how you get your first customer.
Marky is listed on AppSumo, and its YouTube channel links to an AppSumo page. AppSumo describes it as bootstrapped from day one. I found no source on how AppSumo contributed to revenue.

The company ships SEO-style comparison content. One example is a <cite index="3-4,3-8">'Best AI social media post generator' page comparing Marky with Buffer and SocialBee.</cite> No source gives traffic or results from it.
founder_story: The product's own pages and AppSumo name Josiah Coad as founder and CEO, not Arian Adeli. <cite index="44-1,44-2">Marky's own blog lists Josiah Coad as Marky CEO.</cite> TrustMRR's founder field says Arian Adeli. Arian Adeli's public profiles describe him as the founder of Evernomic, <cite index="31-3">a media-first venture studio that builds, backs and acquires media brands and startups.</cite> He is probably the seller or listing contact. This is an inference and no source confirms it.

<cite index="43-5,43-6">Josiah Coad is an Austin-based software engineer. He started Marky while he was at Tesla.</cite> His past roles include <cite index="56-4">Tesla, John Deere, General Motors and Facebook (2019), per a RocketReach profile.</cite>
In his Medium post he says <cite index="47-9">he didn't quit his job until 8 months in, only when he couldn't do both at the same time.</cite>
On AppSumo he wrote: <cite index="41-5,41-7">he had been tinkering since college, and Marky is his first project that actually got traction.</cite>
<cite index="43-4">The podcast page says he grew Marky from a one-person operation to a 12-person team.</cite>
lessons: Sell before you build. He started with Google Sheets, Zapier and about 10 paying customers, then built the software. The founder says to find your first PAYING customer before investing in code (Medium).

Show the result with no signup friction. You paste a website URL and get a month of branded posts, with 30 free posts and no card (pricing page, podcast). Let people see the finished product before they pay.

Sell the part competitors skip. Marky's own pages pitch that it designs the branded image and not just the caption, and offers a white-label tier for agencies, which gives it a $229 plan (about page, pricing page).
criticism: Crowded market. Marky is compared against Buffer and SocialBee, plus many AI post generators. Marky's own comparison page is marketing and not neutral.
Revenue is not profit. The $336K net income figure is a founder-written message on TrustMRR, and I could not verify it independently. TrustMRR shows the profit margin as hidden.
It runs on third-party platforms. The AppSumo listing says <cite index="39-9">it depends on social media APIs (Facebook, etc.) and OpenAI.</cite> A change by either could hit the product.
A user review mentions <cite index="32-6">'Fast and Helpful, AI Needs Work'</cite> as its headline, so AI output quality is a recurring concern.
The business is for sale at $495,000 (2.5x revenue) on TrustMRR. The 'for sale' status and the seller's identity are worth mentioning on screen if you cover it.
facts: TrustMRR (given): $22,204 MRR, $1,016,714 all-time revenue, 478 active subscriptions, 33% MoM growth.

<cite index="39-5">AppSumo lists the founding date as September 1, 2023</cite> and Austin, TX. TrustMRR says July 2023, and a RocketReach/Success.ai-style profile says Jun 2023. Dates conflict, so say 'launched in 2023'.
<cite index="41-9">AppSumo (the listing is dated about Dec 2024) gives a team breakdown of 5 developers, 2 designers, 3 support and 1 marketing/outreach.</cite>

<cite index="12-6">Getlatka says Marky has raised no outside funding.</cite> It lists 8 employees, which conflicts with the AppSumo breakdown above. It also lists $880K revenue for 2025 and a $2.6M valuation, which are unverified third-party estimates.
<cite index="15-1">It schedules to Facebook, Instagram, X, LinkedIn, TikTok, Pinterest and Google Business.</cite>

A recent Marky blog post (about 6 days old) shows it now offers an API and integrations for AI agents and n8n, per <cite index="44-6">'Connect Marky to your AI agent, your code, or your favorite tools'.</cite>
do_not_claim: Do NOT say it is for self-publishing authors. That TrustMRR one-liner contradicts Marky's own site, which targets small businesses and agencies.
Do NOT say Arian Adeli built or founded Marky. Every product source names Josiah Coad.
Do NOT claim profit, net income of $336K, or margin as verified.
Do NOT claim team size as a firm number (sources say 8, 11 or 12).
Do NOT cite the ~200,000 users figure. I could not verify it. Some third-party pages say 30,000+ users, and they are not Marky's official pages.
Do NOT claim Meta Ads or influencers drove growth with numbers. Only the channel names come from TrustMRR.
Do NOT use the $97/$197/$397 pricing. It comes from mymarky.com, a separate site that is apparently for sale and not the official one.
Do NOT claim any viral moment, Product Hunt launch or the AppSumo deal's revenue. I found no source.
research.notes: Two TrustMRR fields don't match the product's own pages. The one-liner says 'self-publishing authors', but mymarky.ai targets SMBs and agencies. The founder field says Arian Adeli, but Josiah Coad is named founder/CEO everywhere else, and Arian runs the venture studio Evernomic. I found no source confirming who the current owner is. Josiah's LinkedIn snippet shows a LangChain role and the phrase 'past founder', so his current involvement is unclear. Don't state this as fact. The pricing page text above is current (Solo $39, Growth $79, Pro $229). Older third-party pages show different prices. I could not find any Product Hunt, Indie Hackers or X build-in-public source for acquisition. The only sourced growth detail is the founder's early-stage approach, so the script should lean on the 'sell before you build', free-30-posts and white-label angles. The 'for sale' price is $495K and the 2.5x revenue multiple comes from TrustMRR.
